transcript:
This message comes from Brex.
If your best finance people are doing expense reports and chasing receipts, it's time to
get Brex AF, agentic finance that eliminates that work before it starts.
Learn more at brex.com/af.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The White House signaled tonight that CNN will be left off Air Force One for President
Trump's trip to Knoxville, Tennessee tomorrow.
The news organization was replaced by conservative outlet Real America's Voice News.
It comes after Trump banned three news outlets from the White House earlier this week, and
a federal judge ordered the president to immediately restore their access, at least for now.
The Supreme Court handed a major defeat to Missouri Republicans in a redistricting case
that could help determine control of Congress.
As NPR's Nina Totenberg reports, the case involves a Republican-friendly map that the
high court had already rejected.
Missouri's Secretary of State, at the urging of President Trump, sought to use a redistricting
plan adopted in 2025, but the state Supreme Court ruled the move unconstitutional and
the U.S. Supreme Court agreed, twice.
After contrary rulings from two lower federal courts, the high court, for the third time
and with definitive language, told Missouri to cease and desist.
The justices noted that they have repeatedly cautioned against lower courts altering election
rules on the eve of an election, and in fact, voting in Missouri has already begun.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump is canceling nearly $1 billion in funding for immigrant services and diversity
initiatives approved by Congress.
He's using a rare power, rescission, the same maneuver Trump used to cut funding to NPR and
PBS last year, typically Congress can review proposed cuts before they take effect, but
Trump made that all but impossible by announcing them.
With just five days left in the federal fiscal year, the Government Accountability Office
has called the maneuver known as pocket rescission illegal.
Utah Valley University has released a long-awaited report on the assassination of Charlie Kirk
showing lapses in security plans.
The conservative activist was shot and killed on the school's campus last September, Caroline
Ballard of member station KUER has more.
The 157-page report by an independent investigator concluded that no one at UVU acted in bad
faith or with willful disregard to others' safety.
But while the university does have safety policies in place, the report found some of
them were "significantly inconsistent."
The school did not complete a formal security assessment or have an event action plan, and
it deferred critical decisions to Kirk's organization Turning Point USA, including the choice to
hold the event outdoors.
Kirk's family said they plan to sue UVU and the state over security failures.
Accused killer Tyler Robinson is set to stand trial for murder.
For NPR News, I'm Caroline Ballard in Salt Lake City.
U.S. stocks rose today after a cool down in oil prices helped release some of the pressure
on Wall Street.
This is NPR News.
Residents on Hawaii's Big Island are bracing for potentially catastrophic flooding from
Hurricane NOLO.
The National Weather Service says tropical storm conditions expected to begin on land
in the evening.
Meanwhile, Mexico is still under the threat of another Pacific hurricane, Polo.
French President Emmanuel Macron says France will send troops to Saudi Arabia to protect
oil supplies, and NPR's Elinor Beardsley reports European nations are afraid that skyrocketing
gas prices could provoke unrest.
"We are going to send military means, soldiers, radar and defense systems, not to engage in
the conflicts," said Macron, "but to protect the site."
Speaking on primetime TV Thursday evening, Macron was referring to the Red Sea port city
of Yanbu, which he called key to getting out more than five million barrels a day, an area
currently threatened by the Houthis.
French news analysts noted with irony that the U.S., which has a long-term commitment
to protect Saudi Arabia, is largely absent while France is stepping in.
Macron also sought to assure the French that they have adequate gas and oil supplies as
winter approaches, and he said Paris will continue diplomacy to try to reopen the Strait
of Hormuz.
Elinor Beardsley in Pure News, Paris.
Volkswagen says it's recalling 2.86 million Volkswagen and Audi branded vehicles as a
precautionary measure over a screw whose failure could cause a loss of steering.
The affected vehicles are the Volkswagen Tiguan, Touran, Golf, Golf Variant and Caddy models
built between 2013 and 2024, and Audi Q3 models.
This is NPR.

topics.text: White House signals CNN will be excluded from Air Force One for Trump's Knoxville trip
Supreme Court rejects Missouri Republicans' redistricting plan for third time, tells state to cease
Trump cancels nearly $1 billion in immigrant services and diversity funding using pocket rescission
Utah Valley University report finds security lapses in Charlie Kirk assassination on campus
U.S. stocks rise after cooling oil prices ease pressure on Wall Street
Hawaii's Big Island residents brace for potentially catastrophic flooding from Hurricane NOLO
French President Macron announces troops deployment to Saudi Arabia to protect oil supplies
Volkswagen recalls 2.86 million vehicles over steering screw failure in multiple models
